data.why: Walmart adding 300 drone delivery sites is concrete, operational news from just five days ago. It avoids the generic $1.5B funding headline that every other sales rep is using.
data.angle: Rapidly rolling out 300 physical launch sites creates an influx of procurement approvals, equipment purchase orders, and supplier invoices.

not_chosen.reason: Over thirty outlets ran the $1.5B funding round this week, so finance leaders will receive dozens of cold emails opening with that exact figure.
Bad news: headline discusses how the company 'nearly died two years ago', which is awkward and negative to bring up.
Bad news: headline focuses on a competitor stock cratering 69% and private secondary market trading.
Job posting for Strategic Finance Manager is from August 2026, making it much older than the current site rollout announcement.
Headcount growth of 27% is a broad metric and less operationally tangible than 300 specific delivery locations.

data.subject: 300 drone sites
data.body:
Hi Mac,

Walmart is adding 300 drone delivery sites with Zipline.

Rolling out that many launch sites usually means a surge of supplier bills and purchase orders to approve across regions. Who is matching and approving all those orders today?

Amgen automated 85% of purchase requisitions through approval with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
